## 2\. Finite exact witness construction and bit costs

The criterion above has a fully explicit witness-generation algorithm. No infinite numerical limit has to be evaluated.

For each \(h\in H\), define

\[
R_h(n)=
c^h\prod_i\frac{\xi_i(n)!}{(\xi_i(n)+h_i)!}.
\]

Because \(h_i\) is fixed, each factorial ratio is a finite product of polynomial factors or their reciprocals. Hence \(R_h(n)\) is an exactly computable rational function of \(n\)\.

Construct

\[
U(n)=\sum_{h\in H}R_h(n)
\]

and

\[
V(n)=
\sum_{\substack{h\in H,r\\h+z_r-y_r\notin H}}
\kappa_r R_h(n)(\xi(n)+h)_{y_r}.
\]

The falling factorial is a polynomial in \(n\), and is exactly zero whenever a source is disabled. Therefore

\[
\frac{B_n}{W_n}
=\frac{V(n)}{U(n)}
=\frac{P(n)}{Q(n)}
\]

for explicitly constructible integer polynomials \(P,Q\), after clearing denominators and choosing the sign of \(Q\) to make its leading coefficient positive.

Under the certified condition \(\Delta<0\),

\[
\deg P<\deg Q.
\]

Let \(q=\deg Q\), let \(q_q>0\) be its leading coefficient, and put \(S_P=\sum_k|p_k|\), where \(p_k\) are the coefficients of \(P\)\.

For positive integer \(n\), choose

\[
N_{\rm flux}(j)=
\max\left\{
1,\
\left\lceil\frac{2\sum_{k<q}|q_k|}{q_q}\right\rceil,\
\left\lceil\frac{4jS_P}{q_q}\right\rceil
\right\}.
\]

For all \(n\geq N_{\rm flux}(j)\),

\[
Q(n)\geq\frac{q_q}{2}n^q,\qquad
\frac{P(n)}{Q(n)}\leq\frac1{2j}.
\]

The case \(P\equiv0\) is handled directly.

To control the stationary mass without computing \(Z_\Gamma\), select a coordinate \(i\) that grows along \(\xi(n)\)\. Then

\[
\xi_i(n)+h_i\geq n
\]

for every \(h\in H\) and integer \(n\geq1\)\.

Put \(C=\sum_i c_i\) and \(K=\lceil2c_i\rceil\)\. The elementary factorial-tail bound gives

\[
W_n\leq |H|\,2^{\lceil2C\rceil+K-n}
\qquad(n\geq K).
\]

Since \(Z_\Gamma\geq w(a)\), an explicit integer \(N_{\rm tail}\) can be obtained from the denominator of the reduced rational number \(w(a)\), ensuring

\[
n\geq N_{\rm tail}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
W_n/Z_\Gamma\leq\tfrac12.
\]

Set

\[
n_j=\max\{N_{\rm flux}(j),N_{\rm tail}\},
\qquad
\boxed{f_j=\mathbf1_{D_{n_j}}.}
\]

Substitution into (4) proves

\[
\frac{\mathcal E(f_j,f_j)}
{\operatorname{Var}_\pi(f_j)}
\leq
\frac{1/(2j)}{1-1/2}
=\frac1j.
\]

The entire construction uses integer and rational arithmetic.

All costs are explicit relative to the finite motif certificate: polynomial

## 3\. Why this does not yet give a total classifier

The finite-cut condition detects a mechanism in which a group of high-population states has progressively smaller outgoing conductance relative to its stationary mass.

The preceding calculation also shows something stronger: whether a *fixed* motif satisfies \(\Delta<0\) depends only on integer growth orders, reaction source complexes, boundary enabling and the chosen offsets. Its truth does not depend on the positive numerical rate constants or concentration values, provided the required complex-balanced class remains the same.

That makes it an effectively testable structural obstruction to a positive gap.

However, the desired decision procedure requires a converse or a separate exhaustive positivity theory.

For example, establishing

\[
\lambda=0
\Longrightarrow
\text{some finite polynomially pumpable motif satisfies }\Delta<0
\]

would turn the present result into a substantially stronger classification tool. **I have not proved this implication.** In particular, an arbitrary sequence of low-energy functions need not, by any result established here, be replaceable with indicators of fixed-size translated patterns.

A zero-gap sequence might involve supports whose shape or cardinality grows with the population scale. Excluding that possibility, or incorporating it into a finite decision procedure, requires a new argument.

Likewise, failure to find a motif cannot serve as a positive-gap certificate. A positive answer still requires a uniform coercivity inequality across every function in the complete form domain.

The available positive path-comparison results of Anderson–Cappelletti–Fan–Kim and negative active-cycle results of Kim–Kim do not establish that converse or provide an exhaustive classifier. citeturn635898view0turn635898view1

Nor can the known undecidability theorems for much broader quantum Hamiltonians be applied without a reduction preserving this problem's specific binomial annihilation operators, rational complex balance and actual population classes. citeturn939695search0

## 4\. Final determination

The investigation establishes a finite, exact, multiscale zero-gap certificate with constructive rational witness families and charged arithmetic costs. It applies in arbitrary dimension, at arbitrary molecularity, across linkage classes, and with boundary-disabled reactions.
